solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: After death, leave that French article in the possession of Elizabeth

indicators.note: whatever is in someone's possession is held inside them, so the earlier words sit within the name

blocks.note: Beth is a short form of the name Elizabeth
que is French for 'that'
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A will-reading scene: after a death, some French article passes into Elizabeth's possession.
explanation.walkthrough: BETH holds QUE + A, giving BE-QUE-A-TH.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath is to leave property to someone in a will, which takes effect after death.

clue.text: Continuous line on map's almost identical on rocky peak

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped
in a down clue, one piece placed on another sits above it, so the first comes before the second

blocks.note: identical means equal
a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A cartographer remarks that a line on the map looks almost the same as a rocky summit.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after map stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The equator is the imaginary unbroken circle drawn round the globe on maps, halfway between the poles.

clue.text: Extremist leaderless sect attracting artist

indicators.note: a group without its leader has lost its head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a cult is a sect
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A fanatic from a sect that has lost its head draws in a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is a person holding extreme views, especially in politics or religion.

clue.text: Central characters in farce bow

indicators.note: the characters in the centre of the word are kept and its ends discarded

blocks.note: the three middle letters of farce

explanation.surface: The main actors in a stage farce take a bow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Central characters' suggests leading roles in the play; here it means the middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bow is a curved shape, as is an arc; the archer's bow takes its name from that curve.

clue.text: Nagged male newsman to capture liaison's latest kiss

indicators.note: the latest part of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept
capturing something means holding it inside, so the newsman surrounds what follows

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
last letter of liaison
a peck is a quick kiss
ED is short for editor

explanation.surface: A man harangues a journalist into catching the final kiss of a love affair on record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newsman' is the editor, a crossword staple; the editor's two letters wrap the kiss and its preceding letter, not the male.
explanation.definitionFit: Henpecked describes a man constantly nagged and bossed about by his wife or partner.

clue.text: Some fox enraged bovine animals

indicators.note: only some of the letters across these words are wanted, a run within them

blocks.note: the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A farmyard picture: a fox has angered the cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxen are cattle, particularly castrated bulls used as draught animals.

clue.text: Guardian maybe supporting cricket side in theory

indicators.note: in a down clue a support stands underneath, so this piece comes after the next one

blocks.note: the on side, or leg side, is one half of a cricket field
The Guardian is a British newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper is backing a cricket team, at least in principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guardian' looks like a protector; the capital G makes it the newspaper. In cricket the field is split into the off side and the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true on paper holds in principle or according to the written plan, though not necessarily in practice.

clue.text: Make a physical effort to pick up Hazel, say, around ten

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so it reads bottom to top
around means surrounding, so the tree's letters wrap the numeral

blocks.note: hazel is an example of a tree
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: Someone strains to lift a woman called Hazel at around ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazel' reads as a woman's name, but 'say' marks it as an example: a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To exert oneself is to make a strenuous physical or mental effort.

clue.text: Depart from capital of Ecuador, stopping early

indicators.note: a word that stops early is cut off before its end, so its last letter goes

blocks.note: Quito is Ecuador's capital city

explanation.surface: A traveller cuts short a stay and leaves the Ecuadorian capital early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' tempts you to take a first letter, E; here it is the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: To quit a place is to leave it, as in quitting the room or the country.

clue.text: Remarkably nice place, former picture house

indicators.note: something done remarkably is out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged unusually

blocks.note: taken as written
PL is an abbreviation for place, as in street names
ex means former

explanation.surface: Someone admires an old cinema that has been turned into a lovely venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former picture house' reads as one phrase, but 'former' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cineplex is a multi-screen cinema complex, and 'picture house' is an old name for a cinema.

clue.text: Unusual ladders around square stand with legs far apart

indicators.note: unusual means not in the normal form, so the letters are rearranged
around means surrounding, so the rearranged letters enclose the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
a T-square is a drawing tool for right angles

explanation.surface: A decorator stands astride a pair of odd ladders set around a square.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of ladders become S-RADDLE, with T slotted in after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to sit or stand with one leg on each side of something, legs spread wide.

clue.text: Fly with speaker somewhere in Devon

blocks.note: to dart is to fly or dash quickly
the mouth is what speaks

explanation.surface: A traveller flies off with a loudspeaker to some Devon spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England; the town sits at the mouth of the river Dart.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmouth is a coastal town in Devon, home of the Britannia Royal Naval College.

clue.text: Papa consumed finely minced spread

blocks.note: P is Papa in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Dad has eaten some finely chopped paste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumed finely minced' reads as one description of eating; the definition starts at 'finely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pâté is a smooth paste of finely chopped meat, fish or vegetables, spread on toast.

clue.text: Merchant recalled scarlet painting?

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so the words are read from end to start

blocks.note: scarlet is a shade of red
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: A dealer remembers a red-toned canvas, the question mark hinting at an uncertain memory.
explanation.walkthrough: RED + ART read backwards gives TRA-DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods, which is what a merchant does.

clue.text: Foreign money church needed during tragedy perhaps

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the church sits inside the next word

blocks.note: a tragedy is one kind of drama
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A church is short of funds during some calamity, and foreign cash is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tragedy' reads as a disaster; 'perhaps' marks it as an example of a stage genre.
explanation.definitionFit: The drachma was the currency of Greece before the euro, so it is money from abroad.

clue.text: Martial art Ken attempted initially with speed

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: first letter of Ken
first letter of attempted
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A man named Ken tried a martial art at first, quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Karate is a Japanese unarmed combat sport using strikes with the hands and feet.

clue.text: Repeat manoeuvres involving variable circus equipment

indicators.note: manoeuvres are moves and repositionings, so the letters are shifted around
involving means taking in, so the rearranged letters include the next one

blocks.note: taken as written
algebra uses x, y and z for unknown values

explanation.surface: A circus acrobat rehearses the same moves again on a swinging bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung from ropes, used by circus acrobats.

clue.text: Tour ocean, regularly seeing killer whale

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A cruise passenger often spots a killer whale while crossing the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is the scientific and common name for the killer whale, a large black-and-white dolphin.

clue.text: Wine and port getting approval from German

blocks.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A German gives his nod to wine and port at dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the fortified drink alongside wine; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white Spanish wine from the La Rioja region.

clue.text: Furious with a girl playing song unaccompanied

indicators.note: playing suggests being in motion, so these letters are moved about

blocks.note: mad means furious
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is angry that a girl is performing a song without any backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a Renaissance part-song for several voices, sung without instruments.

clue.text: Home television advertisement placed within magazine?

blocks.note: in means at home
a television is a TV set

explanation.surface: A TV ad slipped into the pages of a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: an inset is any extra page loosely placed in a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a leaflet or extra sheet put inside a magazine, often an advertising flyer.

clue.text: Jack splashing dosh obtains half-cropped purple equestrian attire

indicators.note: splashing money about scatters it, so these letters are scattered into a new order
cropping half means cutting off half its length, so the back half of the word goes
obtaining means taking in, so the mixed letters hold what follows

blocks.note: J is jack on playing cards
taken as written; dosh is British slang for money
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man called Jack splashes out on purple riding breeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-cropped' removes the second half of the colour; the shortened colour then sits inside the shuffled money, which is British slang. Jodhpur is a city in India, origin of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Jodhpurs are riding trousers, close-fitting below the knee, worn by horse riders.

clue.text: Recognised cutting tool

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of see, perceived
second meaning: a toothed blade for cutting wood

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an acknowledged implement; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the past tense of see, meaning noticed, and the name of a toothed carpentry blade.

clue.text: Susan goes to unknown location in Egypt

blocks.note: Sue is a short form of Susan
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: Susan travels to some secret spot in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Suez is a port city in Egypt at the southern end of the Suez Canal.

clue.text: Indian prince open when reflecting

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things back to front

blocks.note: ajar means slightly open

explanation.surface: An Indian prince becomes open-minded when thinking things over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflecting' reads as pondering, but it signals a mirror image.
explanation.definitionFit: A raja, or rajah, is an Indian king or prince.

clue.text: Question European in Ritz waving gun

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the hotel name
waving makes things move about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: how is a question word
E is the abbreviation for European
taken as written; the Ritz is a London hotel

explanation.surface: A European guest at the Ritz is questioned while brandishing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short artillery piece that fires shells at a high angle.
